name: Udupi

demographics.note: All demographic figures are Census 2011 unless stated. Karnataka sex ratio of 1094 is among the highest in the state.

economy.priceBasis: Per capita NDDP at current prices
economy.gddpCompositionNote: PROXY ONLY — Karnataka state-average sectoral shares, not a district-measured split. Karnataka DES does not publish sector shares at district level in the district GDDP tables. Do not cite as Udupi-specific.
economy.growthRateNote: Not available at district level from DES; left at 0 rather than estimated.

perCapitaIncome.stateRankNote: Exact district rank not yet pulled from the Economic Survey district table. Udupi's PCI (Rs 5.30L, 2023-24) is well above the Karnataka average (Rs 3.40L), so it sits in the upper group, but the precise rank is unverified.

hdi.source: Karnataka State Human Development Report 2022 (Dept. of Planning, Programme Monitoring & Statistics)

keySectors: Higher education & health sciences (MAHE Manipal — Institution of Eminence; Nitte University)
Marine fisheries (Malpe and Gangolli fishing harbours)
Thermal power generation (UPCL Padubidri/Nandikoor, 1,200 MW, Adani Power)
Cashew processing (cluster concentrated in Kundapura taluk)
Plantation & horticulture crops (areca nut, coconut, cashew) and paddy
Banking & financial services (birthplace of Corporation Bank and Syndicate Bank)
IT & digital services (Robosoft Technologies, Manipal Digital Systems)
Temple, beach and coastal tourism (Sri Krishna Temple Udupi, Malpe, Kaup, Maravanthe)
Red clay roofing tiles (Mangalore tile) and coconut oil milling
strengths: HDI 0.665 — ranked 4th of 30 Karnataka districts (State HDR 2022), above the state average of 0.644
Per capita income Rs 5.30 lakh (2023-24, current prices) vs Karnataka average Rs 3.40 lakh — roughly 1.6x the state average
Sex ratio 1094 females per 1000 males, among the highest in Karnataka and far above the national 943 (Census 2011)
Literacy 86.24%, well above the Karnataka average (Census 2011); PLFS 2023-24 estimates 86.51%

MAHE Manipal: Institution of Eminence, NIRF 2025 rank 3 among universities, NAAC A++, 30,000+ students from 60+ countries, 3,000+ faculty and ~10,000 support staff — a large, counter-cyclical export-earning services base
Malpe is one of the largest fishing harbours on the Karnataka coast; Gangolli is the district's second major harbour
UPCL Padubidri thermal plant: 1,200 MW (2x600 MW) operational since 2010/2012, on a KIADB-notified industrial area, with 25-year PPAs covering ~90% of capacity
Established cashew processing cluster in Kundapura taluk with modernised, partly automated units and export presence
Deep banking penetration — undivided South Canara (Udupi + Dakshina Kannada) is called the 'cradle of banking in India'; Corporation Bank (1906) and Syndicate Bank (1925) were both founded in Udupi
Forest and tree cover at 63.64% of geographical area (2023) — high ecological base for watershed and eco-tourism value
Very high rainfall (5,135.5 mm in 2024-25) supporting plantation agriculture
Strong domestic tourism footfall — 78.05 lakh domestic visitors recorded in 2016
NH-66 coastal highway and Konkan Railway connectivity; Mangaluru International Airport ~35 km from the district's southern industrial belt
challenges: Education sub-index is the weakest component of Udupi's HDI (0.566 vs health 0.76 and income 0.684) — mean-years-of-schooling index is only 0.492 despite high literacy
Heavy economic concentration: MAHE/Manipal and the UPCL power plant account for a large share of formal-sector activity, creating single-employer exposure
Manipal's local economy is tied to the academic calendar — trade and services revenue compresses into roughly nine months of the year
Coastal erosion and monsoon damage along the shoreline affect fishing settlements and coastal infrastructure

UPCL runs on imported coal, exposing generation economics to global coal prices and foreign exchange movement; the proposed 2x800 MW expansion has faced local opposition and has not moved past pre-construction
Both banks founded in the district have since been merged away (Corporation Bank into Union Bank, Syndicate Bank into Canara Bank, 2020), removing district-headquartered financial institutions
Out-migration of working-age population to Bengaluru and the Gulf; district population grew only 5.85% in 2001-11, the slowest phase on record
Deaths (12,051) were close to live births (13,460) in 2023, indicating an ageing population structure
Karnataka DES does not publish district-level sectoral GDDP shares or growth rates, limiting the ability to track structural change in Udupi
Marine fisheries face seasonal fishing bans, fuel cost volatility and stock pressure; catch and value data are collected at harbour level rather than published as district accounts
opportunities: Leverage MAHE's incubators (MUTBI) and the existing IT base (Robosoft, Manipal Digital Systems) to build a coastal tech and health-tech cluster outside Bengaluru
Medical value travel and health-sciences services built on Kasturba Medical College and the Manipal hospital network
Value-addition and branding in cashew — organic certification, ISO/HACCP upgrades and direct export channels from the Kundapura cluster
Cold chain and processing capacity at Malpe and Gangolli to move from fresh fish sales toward higher-value marine exports
Areca nut and coconut value chains — coconut oil, desiccated products, areca leaf and fibre-based packaging
Coastal and island tourism — Karnataka Maritime Board has flagged the islands off Malpe as largely untapped for tourism investment
Convert the very high rainfall and forest cover into watershed, micro-hydel and eco-tourism assets
Retain student and graduate talent locally through GCC/offshore development centres, addressing the nine-month revenue cycle
Revive district-level financial services depth (NBFCs, co-operatives, fintech) building on the region's banking heritage

dataCompleteness.verificationNote: Demographics, district GDDP/NDDP/PCI and HDI are sourced and cross-checked. Sectoral GDDP composition is a state-average proxy. Sector narrative items are sourced but not quantified at district level. No roadmap, investment pipeline, credit, MSME or KPI-target tables are included because no verified district-level figures were available for them.

removedInThisRevision: 'Padubidri deep-water port, 10 MMTPA, Rs 4,000 Cr' — no such project could be verified. The real asset at Padubidri is the UPCL 1,200 MW thermal power plant. Malpe is a minor port and fishing harbour under the Karnataka Maritime Board.

'Coffee plantations, 45,000 ha' (later reduced to 6,000 ha) — unverified. Karnataka DES/Indiastat list Udupi's principal crops as paddy, coconut, cashew and areca nut. 45,000 ha approximates state-level coffee area, not Udupi's.
'Cashew processing — 2nd largest in India, 80,000 MT/year, 15,000+ workers' — unverified. A real cluster exists in Kundapura taluk, but no district capacity or employment total could be sourced.
'1M+ annual visitors' — understated and unsourced. Indiastat records 78,05,403 domestic and 1,474 foreign visitors for 2016.
'Coconut plantations 30,000 ha', '12,000+ fishermen', 'Rs 150 Cr seafood exports', '90 km coastline', 'Rs 500 Cr tourism revenue', '5,000+ hotel rooms' — all unsourced district-level figures.

roadmap / industries / creditData / msme / investments / kpis / roleDashboards blocks — these contained invented budgets, job counts, progress percentages and revenue projections presented with false source attribution and 'high' confidence labels. Removed rather than corrected.
